systems.name: creative-core
systems.description: The pure-Swift engines of a Mac-native creative suite: the FlareCore animation engine plus the shared CoreColor, CoreRaster, CoreAsset, CoreCatalog, CoreRender and CoreRenderMetal modules. Linux-safe, Foundation only, except CoreCatalog, which uses GRDB over the system SQLite, and CoreRenderMetal, which uses Metal on macOS and builds empty on Linux. The Mac apps live in other repos.

containers.name: FlareCore library
containers.description: The FlareCore Swift package (Sources/FlareCore). Value types only, Codable and Sendable, and nothing crashes on untrusted input.

components.name: Document and Command Engine
components.description: The document model (Document > Scene > Layer > Shape, keyframe tracks, fills, text shapes, ruler guides, the swatch palette, metadata, frame labels) and its ModelError; LayerOwner, which addresses a scene's or a symbol's layer list; the Command protocol and CommandEngine with exact undo/redo, groups, coalescing, an undo depth limit and layer-scoped validation for single-layer commands; the CommandRegistry that decodes any command from a JSON envelope; the built-in command families (scene, layer, shape, text, keyframe, label, guide, swatch, metadata), with the stroke, path and duplicate-layer commands, scene canvas, rename and reorder; and the .flare v1 file format with validation. Every document change goes through a Command.

components.name: Geometry
components.description: 2D affine Matrix, the Transform (position, scale, rotation; scene space is y down) layers and instances use, axis-aligned Rect, vector Paths with line, quadratic and cubic segments and their affine transform, tight shape bounds, and point hit testing (even-odd and nonzero fill, strokes, through instances). The per-frame render list of a scene or symbol: one walk that gives the layer and instance tree exporters write and the flat paint-order items (matrix, multiplied opacity, inherited lock, address) the stage draws; the queries over it (topmost hit with a tolerance, marquee, world bounds with stroke); and the path builders for rectangles, ellipses, polygons and stars. Nothing here traps on non-finite input.

components.name: Timeline
components.description: Frame/time conversion, keyframe interpolation with binary-search segment lookup, easing curves (linear, cubic bezier, hold), sampling a layer's property values at a frame for rendering and export, and onion skin frames around the playhead.

components.name: Export
components.description: Exporters that turn a scene into other formats: one frame as an SVG document, a scene as a Lottie JSON document with animated position, scale, rotation and opacity, and gradient stop alpha, and the frame plan (numbers, times, pixel sizes, file names) for a numbered PNG sequence. Output is byte-stable and throws on non-finite values.

components.name: Symbols
components.description: Reusable symbol definitions and their instances on layers: how an instance maps the host timeline onto the symbol's own timeline, the add/remove/rename/convert-to-symbol commands, the instance add, remove, move and playback commands, and the check that rejects symbols that contain themselves.

components.name: State Machine
components.description: Interactive state machines: states that play a frame range of a scene, transitions fired by named triggers, typed bool/number inputs with transition conditions, the issues query that lists every broken rule and unreachable state without throwing, the format-layer check over it that FlareFormat.validate runs, the machine, state, transition and input commands, and the player that steps a machine at run time.

containers.name: CoreColor library
containers.description: Shared color module (Sources/CoreColor): color spaces and conversions for every app. Linux-safe, Foundation only, no dependencies.

components.name: Color Spaces
components.description: Color3 and conversions between sRGB, linear sRGB, Display P3, XYZ D65 and OKLab through one shared transfer curve (public as TransferCurve, which CoreRaster's sRGB tone encoding uses); 8-bit display tables (DisplayTransfer: table decode and threshold encode for sRGB and Display P3); ColorError.

containers.name: CoreRaster library
containers.description: Shared raster module (Sources/CoreRaster): pixel buffers, compositing and image operations for Photo, Library and Halo. Linux-safe, Foundation only.

components.name: Pixel Buffer
components.description: PixelBuffer and RGBA: validated sizes, bounds-checked access, premultiply helpers; conversion to and from 8-bit sRGB or Display P3 display bytes through CoreColor's display tables, of the whole buffer or of one region without a crop copy; the tile grid for per-tile storage and paint, and TileDiff for tile-by-tile undo; RasterError.

components.name: Compositing
components.description: W3C blend modes and source-over compositing with opacity on premultiplied pixels, in place on the backdrop one row at a time (an opaque normal row at full opacity is copied in), with free functions that composite a copy.

components.name: Image Operations
components.description: Masks, resampling, crop, quarter turns and rotation by any angle with the straighten crop, blur, tone adjustments and histograms (levels, curves and histograms on linear or sRGB-encoded values) and cloning from an offset through a mask over PixelBuffer.

containers.name: CoreAsset library
containers.description: Shared asset module (Sources/CoreAsset): the Asset and AssetRef model every app imports and exports, and its manifest.json codec. Linux-safe, Foundation only, no dependencies.

components.name: Asset Model
components.description: Asset (id, kind, name, tags, version, source app, payload ref), AssetRef (id, version) and the manifest codec with size limits; AssetError.

containers.name: CoreCatalog library
containers.description: Shared catalog module (Sources/CoreCatalog): photo and metadata catalog over SQLite, used by Library and the shared asset library. Linux-safe; depends only on GRDB.

components.name: Catalog Store
components.description: The catalog schema and its migrations, record types and queries (smart collection rules compiled to SQL) over a GRDB database; CatalogError, which GRDB's errors map to.

containers.name: CoreRender library
containers.description: Shared render module (Sources/CoreRender): the RenderBackend contract every app's Model draws through, its backends (a fake for tests, and the CPU backend over CoreRaster, the pixel reference), RenderDispatcher, which routes each op to a backend by support and health, the parity harness, and the Linux-safe parts of the Metal backend (capabilities, tiling math, cache keys). Linux-safe, Foundation only.

components.name: Render Contract
components.description: The RenderBackend contract: the op families (RenderOp), the one error type (RenderError), surface handles (RenderSurface), the tone adjustments the adjust op takes (ToneAdjustment), the RenderBackend protocol, the blend-mode-to-family and raster-error mappings every backend shares, the SurfaceStore that holds a backend's PixelBuffers behind one lock and updates one in place, and FakeBackend, the recording test double.

components.name: CPU Backend
components.description: CPUBackend, the CPU RenderBackend and pixel reference (Sources/CoreRender/CPU), supporting every op family: its surfaces are PixelBuffers held in the shared SurfaceStore; surface, read and release go through the SurfaceStore; display and composite (every blend mode, gated by its family) are the CoreRaster calls themselves, composite blending the stored backdrop in place under the store's lock so composites onto one surface apply one at a time, and crop, rotate, resample, blur, unsharp, each tone adjustment and masked clone (CPUBackend+Ops) each call the CoreRaster method they name and return a new surface. CoreRaster errors map to RenderError.raster with the same message.

components.name: Render Dispatcher
components.description: RenderDispatcher, the routing between backends: each op goes to the preferred backend when it supports the op's family and is healthy, else to the CPU backend, recording the last fallback (op family and reason, unsupported or unhealthy). A surface made by the other backend is read and re-uploaded to the routed backend first, so a fallback never changes a pixel.

components.name: Metal Support
components.description: The Metal backend's Linux-safe parts (Sources/CoreRender/Metal): binary16 half-float conversion for filling rgba16Float textures from Float32 buffers and reading them back; MetalCapabilities, the proven op set and health state that RenderDispatcher reads; SurfaceTiling, the 256 px tile grid a surface's textures follow, on CoreRaster's shared tile math, with the tiles a rect touches and the default memory budget (half the working set, at least one tile); PipelineKey, the identity of one cached compute pipeline (op family plus a short identifier variant) and the kernel function name it maps to; DisplayTable, CoreColor's DisplayTransfer byte rules as Float thresholds (the curve's and the alpha's, plus CoreColor's own linear sRGB to Display P3 matrix, DisplayTransfer.p3FromLinearSRGB, as Float) that the Metal display kernel uploads, with encode, the kernel's per-pixel rule in Swift, outputFits, display's check against the device's buffer limit, and the CPU backend's error for a non-display space; and TileMap, the pixel map of a crop or quarter turn between two tilings (crop rectangles checked with CoreRaster's messages) split into tile-to-tile copy pieces, refusing a tiling of another size than the source it was made for; and CompositeMap, the overlap of a source placed on a backdrop at an integer offset (CoreRaster's in-place composite clip, safe for any Int offset) split into tile-to-tile pieces, with CoreRaster's opacity check; and ResampleTable, one resample axis's taps (CoreRaster's public ResampleFilter.taps, clamp-to-edge indices and weights normalised in Double, flattened and stored as Float, the identity for an unchanged length) as flat arrays the Metal resample kernel uploads, with apply, the kernel's sum in Swift, and peakPixels, the largest buffer a resample allocates, checked against the device limit; and AdjustTable, every tone adjustment as CoreRaster's own adjustment on a probe line run through the CPU backend (per-channel gains for exposure and white balance, a square-root-spaced table over 0...1 with octave tables of the CPU's values outside it, 2^-24 to 2^40 on each side, read by exponent bits and interpolated on the mantissa, an overflowing octave holding the largest finite Float, for levels, curves and contrast, or a gain per Rec. 709 luminance, constant outside 0...1, for highlights/shadows) that the Metal adjust kernel uploads, with apply and map, the kernel's rule in Swift; and OpaqueRows, CoreRaster's opaque-row copy rule (.normal at opacity exactly 1, every stored alpha of the row exactly 1) as per-row flags of a composite piece split into maximal blit and kernel row runs; and BlurTable, CoreRaster's Gaussian blur kernel mirrored exactly (2 ceil(3 sigma) + 1 weights normalised in Double, stored as Float, sigma 0 the single weight 1, CoreRaster's sigma checks and messages, every weight pinned by test to CoreRaster's blur of an impulse) that the Metal blur kernel uploads, with apply, the kernel's clamp-to-edge sum in Swift; and UnsharpRule, the amount and threshold the Metal unsharp kernel uploads (as two Floats), with CoreRaster's amount, threshold and overflow checks and messages, and apply, the kernel's own Float32 rule per premultiplied component (a difference from the blur strictly over Float(threshold) moves it by amount times the difference, one fused multiply-add), which agrees with CoreRaster's Double rule to Float rounding, a difference that close to the threshold taking either branch. Pure Swift integer and floating-point math, no Metal import, so it builds, tests and mutates on Linux.

components.name: Parity Harness
components.description: How one RenderBackend is measured against another (Sources/CoreRender/Parity): ParityTolerance (byte and linear bounds, .standard and .nonSeparable); ParityHarness.compare, which checks two results' sRGB display bytes through CoreRaster's rgba8 and their linear premultiplied Floats over visible pixels and names the worst pixel; ParityHarness.compare(golden:), the bytes-only compare of a result against a golden, encoded in the golden's color space (both compares count only alpha where both alpha bytes are 0); ParityPack, the layout of the packed CPU goldens (ParityPack.all, each sample's band of rows) and ParityGolden.band(from:op:sample:) and rows(_:), which copy one sample's golden out of its pack; the deterministic sample set per RenderOp (seeded buffers plus alpha 0, subnormal alpha, opaque rows and sources off every edge) and rendering a sample on any backend; and golden files (raw rgba8 bytes beside a JSON header), validated as untrusted input.

containers.name: CoreRenderMetal library
containers.description: Metal render module (Sources/CoreRenderMetal): the Metal RenderBackend, macOS only. The one module allowed to import Metal; every file is wrapped in #if canImport(Metal), so Linux builds it empty.

components.name: Metal Backend
components.description: The Metal RenderBackend: a device and its command queue, capability state behind one lock that no GPU wait holds (fail; recover, which clears a failure only after the health probe passes on a new queue; a health probe that runs one kernel from its own memo; recordCompletion, which marks the backend unhealthy on any command-buffer error; a failed texture allocation also marks it unhealthy), tiled rgba16Float surfaces (one texture per 256 px tile, shared storage on unified memory and managed on a discrete GPU) uploaded from Float32 pixel buffers through HalfFloat with every component clamped to the finite half range and downloaded back, tile eviction under a memory budget (budgetBytes, half the device's recommended working set by default: the least recently used tiles move to a CPU shadow until residentBytes fits, and a read merges resident tiles with shadows), and the pipeline cache: MSL compiled at runtime from string constants, once per PipelineKey (variants from outside go through PipelineKey.validated), memoised in process with Metal's own shader cache across launches; cacheURL is reserved and nothing is read, written or deleted there. Display encode (MB-3, enabled at init) runs the display_encode kernel over resident tiles, reading DisplayTable's thresholds and P3 matrix, and encodes evicted tiles from their shadows on the CPU. Transform (MB-7) runs on the GPU: crop as blit copies and quarter turns as a rotate kernel, piece by piece from TileMap into a new surface (an evicted source tile is copied from its shadow through a temporary texture), with the CPU backend's errors for an invalid crop. Normal composite (MB-4, enabled at init on a read-write tier 2 device only) runs the composite_normal kernel in place on the backdrop's tiles, piece by piece from CompositeMap, with CoreRaster's sourceOver rule, opacity check and clip (an evicted backdrop tile is brought back to a texture first and the budget enforced after; a source that is the backdrop is read from a snapshot). The eleven other separable modes (MB-5) run as variants of the same in-place path, one blendSeparable_<mode> kernel each with CoreRaster's blend formula, with .blendSeparable enabled at init on a read-write tier 2 device (MB-6). Hue, saturation, color and luminosity (MB-9) run through the same in-place path as one blendNonSeparable_<mode> kernel each with CoreRaster's Lum, Sat, SetLum, SetSat and ClipColor, but .blendNonSeparable is not enabled at init (MB-10) and the public composite throws unsupported for those modes; a package parity hook enables the family on a read-write tier 2 device. The opaque-row fast path (MB-6): under .normal at opacity exactly 1, the rows of a piece whose stored Float16 source alphas are all exactly 1 (read from the source tile, resident or staged) are copied onto the backdrop tile with blits instead of the kernel, split by OpaqueRows, with pixels equal to the CPU backend's copy. Resample (MB-8) runs bilinear and lanczos3 on the GPU as two separable passes of ResampleTable over whole-image float4 buffers in the CPU's pass order (the source read like `read`, resident tiles merged with shadows, and uploaded from the CPU), scattered into a new surface with components clamped to the finite half range; an invalid size throws the CPU backend's error, and a valid size whose largest buffer is over the device's maxBufferLength throws unsupported(.resample) with the backend still healthy, so the caller resamples on the CPU backend. Adjust (MB-13, MB-14; .adjust enabled at init) runs every tone adjustment (exposure, levels, curves, white balance, contrast, highlights/shadows) through the adjust_tone kernel tile by tile into a new surface, reading AdjustTable's per-channel gains, per-channel table with its two octave tables or luminance gain table on unpremultiplied values with CoreRaster's alpha guard (an evicted source tile through a temporary texture) and the CPU backend's errors for invalid parameters. Gaussian blur (MB-11) runs as two separable blur_pass passes of BlurTable over whole-image float4 buffers in the CPU's order (across, then down) with clamp-to-edge taps, scattered into a new surface by the resample scatter kernel; sigma 0 returns the pixels unchanged and an invalid sigma throws the CPU backend's error. Unsharp mask (MB-12) runs in one command buffer as blur_pass across the rows and then blur_unsharp, which finishes the blur down the columns and sharpens each premultiplied component in Float32 with UnsharpRule's parameters (the rule UnsharpRule.apply mirrors), scattered into a new surface; invalid parameters and an overflowing result throw the CPU backend's errors; .blur is enabled at init, and blur and unsharp throw unsupported while the backend is unhealthy and, with the backend still healthy, for a valid image whose whole-image buffer is over the device's maxBufferLength, so the caller runs them on the CPU backend. Clone through a mask (MB-15; .retouch enabled at init) packs the source, read like `read`, and the mask's coverage into whole-image buffers and runs retouch_clone into each tile of a new surface with CoreRaster's clone rule, the CPU backend's errors in its order, and offsets whose sources are all off the image returning the pixels unchanged; an image over maxBufferLength throws unsupported, and so does clone while the backend is unhealthy. Non-separable blends stay off at init until MB-10.

systems.name: GRDB.swift
systems.description: External: SQLite toolkit for Swift (groue/GRDB.swift), pinned exact in Package.swift. Links the system SQLite; on Linux that needs libsqlite3-dev. Approved for CoreCatalog only.

relationships.description: shapes and layers are placed with Transform and Path
keyframe tracks carry easing; commands keep keyframes sorted
samples layer properties at a frame
writes transforms as matrices and shapes as paths
reads scenes, layers, shapes and fills
symbols hold layers and change the document through commands
states play frame ranges of a document's scenes; validated by FlareFormat
pixels carry colors in CoreColor's spaces
opens databases, runs migrations and queries through GRDB
backends hold surfaces as CoreRaster pixel buffers and the parity harness compares them; the CPU backend draws through CoreRaster's operations
display encodes into CoreColor's color spaces
implements the RenderBackend contract, measured against the CPU backend as it lands
